description: Speak JSON-RPC to the INSTALLED bridge from a directory that is not the project, and prove that the per-call `cwd` tool input is what makes it answer for the project.
why: Plan item 4g / ADR-0045 D6. Under an Agent Plugins client the server's cwd is the plugin root. Without `cwd`, a tool reads no project and reports that cleanly — the worst failure. The contrast pair here (same tool with and without cwd, from a foreign directory) is the only shape that proves the input is load-bearing rather than decorative. Spawned, not required: the framing loop and the deployed copy are what is measured.

steps.why: The seed is a real PAN project to the installed engine — otherwise every later assertion would be measuring the seed, not the bridge.

id 1: every tool advertises cwd. id 2 vs 3: the SAME tool from the SAME foreign directory succeeds only when cwd names the project — the load-bearing contrast (roadmap analyze errors on a directory with no roadmap, by design). id 4: a second tool for good measure. id 5: a relative cwd is a bad REQUEST (-32602), not a spawn with a bad root.
